section_summary.extract_value: This section describes two hierarchical moderated regression models testing BMI as a moderator of the association between body dissatisfaction and positive body image measures. For body appreciation, the full model explained 22% of variance, with BMI as the strongest predictor and current-personal ideal body size discrepancy contributing an additional 2.3% of variance; no interaction terms were significant. For body image flexibility, the model explained 34% of variance with BMI remaining the strongest negative predictor and accounting for a larger proportion of variance compared to body appreciation, while current-personal ideal body size discrepancy also contributed unique variance.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents hierarchical moderated regression analyses examining how BMI and body size discrepancies (measures of body dissatisfaction) predict body appreciation and body image flexibility. Table 2 shows results for body appreciation (N=223), where BMI emerged as the strongest negative predictor (β = -0.43), and the discrepancy between current and personal ideal body size contributed additional variance. The full model explained 22% of variance in body appreciation, and none of the proposed interaction terms contributed unique variance.
